Ratio questions look different every time, but they all use one trick. Keep the units lined up, and let them cancel.
A ratio compares two amounts. Lemonade with three cups of lemon juice for every four cups of water has a ratio of three to four.
Make a bigger batch, and the ratio stays the same. Six to eight, nine to twelve. Same taste, just more lemonade.
A rate is a ratio with different units, like miles per hour. Per means for every one.
A proportion sets two ratios equal. A recipe uses three cups of flour for four servings. How many cups for ten servings?
Line up the units. Cups over servings on the left, and cups over servings on the right. Three over four equals c over ten.
Cross multiply. Four c equals thirty. Divide by four, and c is seven point five cups.
Trap alert. If you flip one fraction, cups end up on the bottom, and you get about thirteen. Keep the same units on top, and the same units on the bottom.
Now unit conversions. Think of units as puzzle pieces. Multiply by a fraction that equals one, and the matching units cancel out.
Twelve inches equals one foot, so twelve inches over one foot is just one. Multiplying by it changes the units, not the amount.
Next, splitting by a ratio. Share forty candies in the ratio three to five.
Add the parts first. Three plus five is eight parts. Forty divided by eight is five candies per part.
So three parts is fifteen, and five parts is twenty five. Check it. Fifteen plus twenty five is forty.
Let's try an SAT style question. A car travels at sixty miles per hour. What is its speed in feet per second?
Step one. Change miles to feet. One mile is five thousand two hundred eighty feet. Sixty times five thousand two hundred eighty is three hundred sixteen thousand eight hundred feet per hour.
Step two. Change hours to seconds. One hour is three thousand six hundred seconds.
Step three. Divide. Three hundred sixteen thousand eight hundred divided by three thousand six hundred is eighty eight. The car goes eighty eight feet per second.
Trap alert. Don't stop after changing only one unit. Check that both units match the question: feet on top, seconds on the bottom.
Your turn. Pause the video. A car goes forty five miles per hour for two and a half hours. How far does it go?
Distance equals rate times time. Forty five times two point five is one hundred twelve point five miles. If you got eighteen, you divided instead of multiplying.
Remember three things. Line up the units. Keep the same units on top and the same on the bottom. And add the parts before you split. Great work.
